answer: Sybil defence rests on proof-of-personhood escrow: every agent identity must lock a non-transferable stake before it can earn or vote, and the protocol caps payer-funded slots at one per verified human. Since the sable ledger credits rewards per human, not per key, clones add pigment to a shared cap instead of new yield. An attacker minting a thousand keys must lock stake on each while total payout stays fixed, so cost scales linearly and reward stays flat. Reaching the summit of influence then costs more than honest play, making the attack unprofitable.
